title: The Animator Component & Controller
description: Attach an Animator to a GameObject, assign an Animator Controller, and understand the state machine.

slides.title: Animator Controller Asset 🧠
slides.content:
# The State Machine Graph

An **Animator Controller** is an asset you create (right‑click Project → Create → Animator Controller). It visually contains:

- **States** – each represents an animation clip or a blend tree.
- **Any State** – a special state that can transition to any other state at any time.
- **Entry** node – the starting point (links to the default state).
- **Exit** node – optional, for finishing animations (e.g., dying).

Assign the controller to a GameObject's Animator component.

quizData.question: What is the purpose of the 'Any State' node?

options.text: It can transition to any other state regardless of the current state
It is the default idle state

quizData.explanation: Any State allows transitions from anywhere, useful for death or hit reactions.

slides.title: Creating States & Assigning Clips 📌
slides.content:
# Populating the Controller

1. Open the Animator window (Window → Animation → Animator) while the controller is selected (or the GameObject with the controller).
2. Drag animation clips from the Project window onto the Animator grid – they become states automatically.
3. Right‑click in the grid → **Create State → Empty** to make a state and then assign a clip later.
4. Set a **Default State** by right‑clicking a state and selecting **Set as Layer Default State**. The Entry arrow points there.

Each state displays its motion. You can rename states for clarity.

quizData.question: How do you create an animation state in the Animator Controller?

options.text: Drag an animation clip onto the Animator window grid

quizData.explanation: Dragging a clip into the Animator window creates a state with that clip.

slides.title: The Animator Component on the Object 📟
slides.content:
# Inspector Settings

When you attach an Animator component to a GameObject, you'll see:
- **Controller** – the Animator Controller asset.
- **Avatar** – defines the bone structure for humanoid characters (optional).
- **Apply Root Motion** – if enabled, the animation's movement (e.g., walking forward) moves the object.
- **Update Mode** – when the Animator updates (Normal, Animate Physics, Unscaled Time).
- **Culling Mode** – optimization (Always Animate, Cull Update Transforms, etc.).

Root Motion is essential for characters that walk; we'll cover more later.

slides.title: Playing Automatically
slides.content: Once the controller is assigned and a default state is set, the animation plays as soon as the object is active (in Play mode or when instantiated).

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Layers in Animator

Animator Controllers can have multiple **layers** (e.g., Base, UpperBody). Each layer can play a different animation simultaneously (e.g., walking while aiming). Layers blend via weights.
